title: How Large Language Models Systematically Misrepresent American Climate Opinions

bias_targets.methodology: Comparing LLM-generated survey responses using multi-attribute demographic personas against actual human responses to identify compounded misrepresentations at the intersections of race, gender, and political ideology.
Measuring the gap between LLM predictions and human responses for male versus female personas, specifically analyzing how models apply uniform gender assumptions across different racial groups.

Analyzing LLM prediction mismatches for White, Black, Hispanic, and Other non-Hispanic personas to determine if models systematically over- or underestimate climate concern for specific racial groups.
Evaluating how LLMs misrepresent climate opinions across a 5-point political ideology spectrum (from very liberal to very conservative), testing if models compress or distort ideological extremes.
Assessing prediction accuracy and systematic gaps based on the persona's household income category and educational attainment level.
Testing for systematic prediction errors by including the exact age of the respondent in the LLM prompt and regressing the prediction gap on age.
Comparing model predictions for religious versus non-religious personas to identify any systematic misrepresentation of their climate opinions.
Evaluating prediction mismatches based on the geographic region of the persona (Northeast, Midwest, South, West).
